question: How does an ordered list of named qubits determine a unique computational-basis coordinate, and how can an output index be decoded without confusing labels and significance?
result: Bijection between bit tuples and statevector indices
entry: Use 4.1 finite product bases and its finite-basis Born convention; extend the ordered product to n distinguishable qubits. No later permutation/local-operator theorem assumed.
exit: Prove the most-significant-qubit index bijection and its inverse, preserve leading zeros and distinguish qubit labels, tuple positions, basis indices, amplitudes and outcome probabilities.
assumptions: Positive finite qubit count; distinct application labels in declared order
Each qubit basis is ordered0,1; position0 is most significant
Zero-based global statevector index; row-major lexicographic product-basis listing
Pure register vector and finite-basis Born convention from4.1; no measurement update imported
Named labels are application metadata, not a new framework or hardware API
